summary: End-to-end testing of Honnugudi Coffee Trading ERP. Executed 39 backend pytest cases covering auth (login, cookies, invalid creds, /me), masters (parties/products/godowns, market rate), RBAC (admin/operator/finance perms — operator cannot list users or set market rate; finance is 403 on /api/purchases but can create /api/payments), full BUY workflow (multi-item purchase with SOLD+HOLD, buy advance, partial settlement with advance applied), full SELL workflow (dispatch SOLD/HOLD with stock validation, sell advance, sell settlement), payments, reversals (payment reversal succeeds; reversing purchase whose HOLD was settled is blocked; finance cannot reverse), party ledger running balance, and money integrity math. Frontend verified: login, dashboard with all 8 KPI cards, market rate widget (admin-only input) works, navigation across all pages (Masters, Purchases, Dispatches, Advances, Settlements, Payments, Ledgers) renders, purchase bill modal opens with all data-testids present (product/godown SearchSelect, mode-hold toggle, save button), settlements modal launcher present, users tab visible to admin. No page errors. 39/39 backend tests PASS.

minor.issue: CORS_ORIGINS='*' combined with allow_credentials=True is invalid per browser spec — browsers will reject preflight when credentials are needed. Currently frontend works only because same-domain via ingress. Should set CORS_ORIGINS to an explicit origin list when frontend is served from a different domain.
Documents returned still contain internal fields (created_at, active etc). No _id leak (out() renames to id). Non-critical, acceptable.

Uses Python round() (banker's rounding). Problem statement's example says '100.5 kg at ₹250.75/kg = amount_paise 25200375' but correct paise formula yields 2520038 (off by 10x in the spec). Backend math is internally consistent; spec sample value appears typo'd. Verified 100500g * 25075paise/kg /1000 = 2520037.5 -> 2520038, which is what backend returns.

ui_bugs.issue: Reverse link is displayed for purchases that have already-settled HOLD items; clicking will fail with backend 400. UX-wise it should be disabled/hidden or show a tooltip explaining the settlement must be reversed first.

issues: Placeholder '₹/kg' inside dark maroon input has low contrast against very dark background — hard to read; consider lighter placeholder or explicit label

action_items: Consider tightening CORS_ORIGINS to explicit domain list (currently '*' with allow_credentials=True which browsers reject when cookies are actually needed cross-origin).
Hide/disable Reverse link on Purchase and Dispatch rows whose items have settled_qty_g > 0 to avoid confusing error toast.

Confirm intended paise math: spec example says 100.5kg @ ₹250.75 = 25200375 paise, but formula gives 2520038 paise (₹25,200.38). Backend is self-consistent and UI renders ₹25,200.38 correctly. Update spec docs or clarify.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py: cookies use secure=True + samesite='none' — good for cross-site cookie behaviour on HTTPS, but combined with CORS allow_origins='*' will fail in real browsers. Move CORS_ORIGINS to explicit list.
transactions.py create_reversal: correctly guards on settled_qty_g > 0 for purchase/dispatch; correctly decrements settled_qty_g on settlement reversal. Good.
reports.py hold_unpriced pipeline: correctly excludes reversed docs and uses items.settled_qty_g. Good.
core.py stock_balance uses aggregate — correctly signs qty_g (dispatch entries stored as negative). Good.
No mongo _id leakage — all endpoints use out() helper.
Pydantic validation on all bodies, integer paise/grams enforced. Good.
Login lockout: after 5 failed attempts, 15-min lockout — implemented and tested (indirectly via 401 path).
seed_admin: idempotent, updates hash if admin password changed. Good.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for smoke/nav; full CRUD via UI not exhaustively driven — backend flows validate the same code paths

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression test at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py — MUST be run with -n 0 (serialised) because tests share a `state` session fixture; pytest.ini defaults to -n 2 which will scatter fixture across workers and break inter-class ordering. Command: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/backend_test.py -v -n 0 --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml`. Each run creates new TEST_ parties/products/godowns/users with timestamps, so tests are idempotent. All backend flows verified working.
